## Lymphoma case-control variable creation

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
source(here::here("R", "cohort_preparation.R"))
dog_pop <- read.csv(here::here("Data/lymphoma_cohort_241201.csv"))
```

Make sure population has the endpoint in date format (but also only to the year level to match to questinoaire etc. data which only annual)

```{r}
# Remove the excess record-date column and create endpoint values at year and
# month levels. Annual owner questionnaires do not justify day-level matching.
dog_pop <- prepare_cancer_cohort(dog_pop)
```

Datasets to join up to:

-   clinic and deprivation indices

-   Environment

-   lifestyle

-   reproduction

-   comorbidities

-   physical exam

-   medications

Need to create from these (where applicable):

-   early life (SY0-2)

-   rest of life (SY3 +)

-   whole life (SY0-final SY of records)

-   5y prior to endpoint

Had seperate files for all of these datasets for the HSA dataset creation but will add in here for other user of file ease

## Clinic and deprivation indices

created in this file for all the clinics based on 2019 values so can use these again as MDI not updated yet- GRLS clinic and deprivation indices linkup.qmd

```{r}
deprivation <- read.csv(here::here("Output/GRLS_dogs_MDI_2019.csv"))

# Join clinic and owner deprivation onto the cancer cohort by subject ID.
dog_pop_deprivation <- add_deprivation_features(dog_pop, deprivation)
```

## Environment exposures

NB. most of the enviro variables (or possibly all) do not have any missing data ie. they are all encoded 0 or 1 for the questionaires - so there is no 3rd level of "no_records/not_recorded" as with many other variables in the dataset

indoors exposures =

'use_aerosol','use_air_cleaner','use_hepa_filter,'use_moth_balls','use_incense_or_candles','smoke_exposure'

outside house exposures=

'any_treated_weeds','any_treated_insects','any_treated_fertilizer'

```{r}
# Environmental-condition and sleep-location questionnaires are separate source
# tables because sleep location can contain a different number of rows per dog.
source(here::here("Code", "GRLS_functions.R"))
source(here::here("R", "environment.R"))

environment_exposures <- read.csv(
  here::here("Data/environment_conditions.csv"),
  na.strings = c("", "NA")
)
sleep_environment <- read.csv(here::here("Data/environment_sleep_location.csv"),na.strings=c("","NA"))
sleep_environment <- sleep_environment %>% mutate(across(where(is.character), tolower))

```

### Tidy to binary version of ever exposed (equiv of whole life):

Indoor exposures are aerosol use, air cleaners, HEPA filters, moth balls,
incense/candles, and household smoke. Outdoor exposures are treatment of weeds,
insects, and lawns with fertiliser.

For every exposure, the shared function creates indicators and counts for:

- early life (study years 0–2);
- rest of life (study years 3–10);
- whole observed life (study years 0–10); and
- the five years preceding the cancer endpoint.

The sleep-location table remains separate because dogs may have multiple sleep
locations within a questionnaire year.

```{r}
environment_features <- build_environment_binary_features(
  environment_exposures,
  dog_pop_deprivation
)

# Retain the established object names used by the smoke and sleep sections below.
indoors_outdoors <- environment_features$longitudinal %>%
  dplyr::select(-dplyr::all_of(setdiff(names(dog_pop_deprivation), "subject_id")))
dog_pop_deprivation_enviro__early_rest_whole4 <-
  environment_features$exposure_windows
dog_pop_deprivation_enviro5y <- environment_features$within_five_years
```

#### Hours of smoke exposure - early, rest, whole, 5y prior

Rows recorded as "see detail rows" do not contain a usable dosage and are
excluded. The shared helper converts the remaining values to numeric hours and
calculates total exposure in early life, the rest of life, the whole observed
life, and before diagnosis. It also retains the binary five-year exposure
features created above.

```{r}
dog_pop_deprivation_enviro_smoking_all <- build_smoke_dosage_features(
  dog_pop_deprivation_enviro__early_rest_whole4,
  dog_pop_deprivation_enviro5y
)
```

### Sleep location

Lots of dogs have multiple `specific_sleep_location` values in the same record
year. Duplicate rows are removed, but distinct locations are retained. The
three recorded locations are garage, house, and outside; the shared helper
creates early-life, rest-of-life, whole-life, and five-year indicators for each.

The main lifetime sleep location is the uniquely most frequent location. A tie
deliberately stops the analysis so that a subject-matter tie rule can be chosen
rather than silently selecting one location.

```{r}
dog_pop_deprivation_enviro_smoking_sleep_all <-
  build_sleep_location_features(
    sleep_environment,
    dog_pop_deprivation_enviro_smoking_all
  )
```

## Lifestyle

- As with the environmental and sleep data, every dog has lifestyle records, so
  this domain does not use a `not_recorded` or `records_not_available` category.
- The established broad groups are competitive, working, breed/showing,
  miscellaneous, companion/pet, and other. Category precedence remains the same
  as in the original notebook when a recorded role contains more than one term.
- A dog's main lifestyle is its most frequently recorded raw role. For the 403
  dogs with equally frequent roles, all tied roles are retained together and the
  broad category is `multiple`; this replaces the previous order-dependent
  selection of one role.

```{r}
source(here::here("R", "lifestyle.R"))

lifestyle <- read.csv(
  here::here("Data", "lifestyle.csv"),
  na.strings = c("", "NA")
)

dog_pop_deprivation_enviro_smoking_sleep_lifestyle_all <-
  add_lifestyle_features(
    dog_pop_deprivation_enviro_smoking_sleep_all,
    lifestyle
  )
```

## Household exposures

Household features come from `Data/house_details.csv`; residential location
features come from `Data/location_history.csv`. Text is normalized to lower case,
and missing or blank source values are represented as `no_records_available`.

Variables retained from this domain are:

- primary and secondary heating and cooking fuel;
- metal and plastic pipe indicators;
- water source, house type, area type, and mean recorded house age; and
- modal region, state, and owner ZIP.

Free-text fuel descriptions are mapped to the established electric, natural gas,
oil, propane, wood, and renewable groups. The curated spelling variants and
mixed-source descriptions are retained in `R/household.R`.

Pipe indicators combine the structured primary/secondary-house questions with
the curated free-text descriptions. If either structured material question has
no record, the derived material value remains `no_records_available`.

For water, municipal supply means a public water system managed by a local
authority or utility and treated to applicable US drinking-water standards. The
approved broad groups are municipal, groundwater, spring/surface, bottled, and
rainwater/cistern. These grouped values—not the original ungrouped answers—are
used for every derived water-source feature.

Early-life (study years 0–2), rest-of-life (3–10), and whole-life (0–10)
features use the most frequent recorded value. Five-year features use the most
frequent value in the five study years before the cohort endpoint. When values
tie, the output is explicitly `multiple` rather than selecting whichever row
appears first.

Dog `094-000461` has no
`year_in_study_diagnosis_or_final_record_year` in either frozen cancer cohort.
The historical notebook replaced this missing value with 1. The shared workflow
now stops so that the cohort endpoint definition must be corrected explicitly
before an analysis dataset is accepted.

```{r}
source(here::here("R", "household.R"))

house <- read.csv(here::here("Data", "house_details.csv"))
location <- read.csv(here::here("Data", "location_history.csv"))

dog_pop_deprivation_enviro_smoking_sleep_lifestyle_all_house_location2 <-
  build_household_features(
    house,
    location,
    dog_pop_deprivation_enviro_smoking_sleep_lifestyle_all
  )
```

#### Chronic inflam conditions ever in all years of study

```{r}
source(here::here("Code/GRLS_functions.R"))

conditions_in_df_and_list <- intersect(colnames(comorbs_unique),comorbs_to_find)

comorbs_unique_2 <- comorbs_unique %>%
  #get rid of the to_date row for each dog
  filter(to_date !=1) %>%
  #get rid of the NA rows in the dataset - then add in later at the 3044 level to be "no_records_available" across the comorbs
  dplyr::select(-c(relationship_category,year_in_study,record_date,to_date))
###not using currently as want to keep the NA to tidy at end into "no_records_available"
#comorbs_unique_2<- comorbs_unique_2%>%
# replacing NA values with 0 across comorbidity columns
 # mutate_at(vars(3:196), ~replace_na(., 0))


#remove the rows in the comorbs_unique_2 that have got NAs across whole dataset for each dog. then when creating cohort variable at end can recode any of these dogs with no records as "no_records_available" (very few missing records across WHOLE study period, generally just occ year)

cols_to_check <- c(7:21,164:196)
comorbs_unique_2 <- comorbs_unique_2[complete.cases(comorbs_unique_2[, cols_to_check]), ]
#checking all dogs have some records to see if need to code any with "no_records_available" at end - all dogs have comorbs records in their lifetime
comorbs_unique <- unique(comorbs_unique_2$subject_id)

df_result2 <- comorbs_unique_2 %>%
  group_by(subject_id) %>%
  mutate(
    #is there any chronic inflam condition present in at least 1 row for subject id
    chronic_inflam_present_lifetime = if_else(
      rowSums(across(all_of(conditions_in_df_and_list))) > 0 & 
        rowSums(across(all_of(conditions_in_df_and_list), ~ sum(. == 1)) > 1), 
      1, 
      0
    ),
    #how many chronic inflam conditions
    number_comorbs_present_lifetime = if_else(
      chronic_inflam_present_lifetime == 1,
      rowSums(across(all_of(conditions_in_df_and_list))),
      0
    ),
    ,
    #what were the comorbidities
    comorbidities_lifetime = if_else(
      chronic_inflam_present_lifetime == 1,
      apply(across(all_of(conditions_in_df_and_list)), 1, function(x) paste(names(which(x == 1)), collapse = "_")),
      "")
  ) %>%
  ungroup()


```

```{r}
# Function to detect comorbidities for each subject_id based on index range
detect_comorbidity <- function(df, subject_id_col, index_range, comorbidity_groups) {
  # Extract actual column names within the index range
  valid_columns <- colnames(df)[index_range]

  df %>%
    group_by(!!sym(subject_id_col)) %>%  # Group by subject_id
    summarise(across(all_of(valid_columns), ~ any(. == 1), .names = "temp_{.col}"), .groups = "drop") %>%  # Check for 1s
    mutate(
      !!!map(comorbidity_groups, function(cols) {
        # Identify valid columns that exist in the dataset
        matched_cols <- intersect(paste0("temp_", cols), colnames(.))
        
        # Assign "Y" if any value in matched columns is 1, else "N"
        if (length(matched_cols) > 0) {
          ifelse(rowSums(dplyr::select(., all_of(matched_cols))) > 0, "Y", "N")
        } else {
          "N"  # If no matching columns exist, default to "N"
        }
      })
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(-starts_with("temp_"))  # Remove temporary columns
}

# Define comorbidity groups (list of column names matching each category)
comorbidity_groups <- list(
  intestinal_parasitism = intestinal_parasitism,
  tick_borne_parasitism = tick_borne_parasitism,
  other_parasitism = other_parasitism,
  all_parasitism = all_parasitism,
  infectious = infectious,
  orthopaedic = orthopaedic,
  immune_mediated = immune_mediated,
  cardiovascular = cardiovascular,
  gastrointestinal = gastrointestinal,
  inflammatory_other = inflammatory_other,
  chronic_inflammatory = chronic_inflammatory
)

# Apply function to data
GRLS_data <- df_result_restricted %>%
  left_join(detect_comorbidity(df_result_restricted, "subject_id", 5:198, comorbidity_groups),
            by = "subject_id")


#keep only a single row for each patient
# Define the index range of comorbidity columns
comorbidity_index <- c(199:212)  # Keep subject_id out of this list

# Create a second dataframe with one row per subject_id, summarizing only the selected columns - not using this as need to ensure rows with a 1 are preferentially kept

 #   .groups = "drop"
 # )


GRLS_summary <- GRLS_data %>%
  group_by(subject_id) %>%
  arrange(desc(number_comorbs_present_5y)) %>%  # prioritise higher values
  slice(1) %>%  # keep only the top row per subject
  ungroup()


### recode any NA as "no_record_available"
GRLS_summary <- GRLS_summary%>%
  mutate(across(where(~ is.character(.) | is.factor(.)| is.numeric(.)),
                ~ replace(., is.na(.) | . == "", "no_records_available")))
```

```{r}
  dplyr::select(subject_id, all_of(comorbs_single_record))

#
lifetime_comorbs_ever <- comorbs_ever %>%
  group_by(subject_id) %>%
  mutate(
    ## ANY lifetime comorb inflam present
    lifelong_comorb_present = if_else(rowSums(across(all_of(comorbs_single_record))) > 0, 1, 0),
    
    ### NUMBER OF chronic inflam conditions present
    number_lifelong_comorbs_present = rowSums(across(all_of(comorbs_single_record))),
    
    # what were the comorbidities
    lifelong_comorbidities = if_else(
      lifelong_comorb_present == 1,
      apply(across(all_of(comorbs_single_record)), 1, function(x) paste(names(which(x == 1)), collapse = "_")),
      NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

#keep count of comorbs and if present and then only a unique row for each patient
lifetime_comorbs_ever_abr <- lifetime_comorbs_ever %>%
    dplyr::select(c(subject_id,lifelong_comorb_present,number_lifelong_comorbs_present))%>%
  group_by(subject_id) %>%
  arrange(desc(number_lifelong_comorbs_present)) %>%  # prioritise higher values
  slice(1) %>%  # keep only the top row per subject
  ungroup()
```

Grouping the lifelong_comorbidities column into type of condition e.g endocrine, ocular etc based on earlier lists

```{r}

valid_comorbidity_groups <- lapply(comorbidity_groups, function(cols) {
  intersect(cols, colnames(lifetime_comorbs_ever))  # Keep only columns that exist in df
})

# Remove empty comorbidity groups
valid_comorbidity_groups <- valid_comorbidity_groups[lengths(valid_comorbidity_groups) > 0]





# Compute 'lifetime' flags for each comorbidity category
df_lifetime <- lifetime_comorbs_ever %>%
  group_by(subject_id) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), \(x) max(x, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%  # Collapse per patient (1 if present, 0 otherwise)
  mutate(!!!setNames(
    lapply(valid_comorbidity_groups, function(cols) {
      if (length(cols) > 0) {
        as.integer(rowSums(.[cols], na.rm = TRUE) > 0)  # Correctly sum across selected columns
      } else {
        rep(0, n())  # Handle cases where no valid columns exist
      }
    }),
    paste0("lifelong_", names(valid_comorbidity_groups))  # Create new column names
  )) %>%
  select(subject_id, starts_with("lifelong_"))  # Keep only new columns

# View output
print(df_lifetime)
```

Combine the lifetime_comorbs_ever_abr and df_lifetime so that we have counts and groupings of these comorbs:

```{r}
lifelong_data <- lifelong_data %>%

GRLS_summary_lifelong<- lifelong_data %>%

#add in _5y to the GRLS summary columns that are from 5y prior to final record
```

Lifetime comorbs now classify into the parasitism/infectious/cardio/ etc

```{r}
# Apply function to data
GRLS_data_lifetime <- df_result3 %>%

            by = "subject_id")

#add in _5y to the GRLS summary columns that are from 5y prior to final record

#keep only a single row for each patient

# Create a second dataframe with one row per subject_id, summarizing only the selected columns
GRLS_summary_lifetime <- GRLS_data_lifetime %>%
```

Combine lifelong and 5y values into one as consider these comorbs to be permanent once diagnosed:

```{r}

    immune_mediated_5y2=pmax(lifelong_immune_mediated,immune_mediated_5y,na.rm=TRUE),
    gastrointestinal_5y2=pmax(lifelong_gastrointestinal,gastrointestinal_5y,na.rm=TRUE),
    inflammatory_other_5y2=pmax(lifelong_inflammatory_other,inflammatory_other_5y,na.rm=TRUE),
    chronic_inflammatory_5y2=pmax(lifelong_chronic_inflammatory,chronic_inflammatory_5y,na.rm=TRUE))

#remove the earlier 5y columns and just keep the ones where lifelong + 5y ar ecombined
```

Create YN and counts for all cancers and malig

NB. indices may no longer work as have now removed benign cancer variables due to inaccuracies

```{r}
comorbs_neoplasia_2 <- conditions_neoplasia %>%
  filter(to_date != 1)%>%
  dplyr::select(-other_specify)

#for next step of 5y

  filter(to_date != 1)%>%
  dplyr::select(-other_specify)
#remove rows where comorbs NA
cols_to_check <- c(6:40)
comorbs_neoplasia_2 <- comorbs_neoplasia_2[complete.cases(comorbs_neoplasia_2[, cols_to_check]), ]


#check if any dogs have no neoplasia records - all do have some records at least for lifetime calcs
unique_cancer <- unique(comorbs_neoplasia_2$subject_id)
comorbs_neoplasia_2$all_cancers_count_lifetime <- 0
comorbs_neoplasia_2$malig_cancers_count_lifetime <- 0

# Loop through the cancer columns by index
for (col_index in cancer_columns) {

  # Count for all cancers
  comorbs_neoplasia_2$all_cancers_count_lifetime <- comorbs_neoplasia_2$all_cancers_count_lifetime + (comorbs_neoplasia_2[[col_name]] == 1)
  
  # Count for all cancers
  comorbs_neoplasia_2$all_cancers_count_lifetime <- comorbs_neoplasia_2$all_cancers_count_lifetime + (comorbs_neoplasia_2[[col_name]] == 1)
  
  # Count for malignant cancers
  if (col_name %in% malig_cancers) {
    comorbs_neoplasia_2$malig_cancers_count_lifetime <- comorbs_neoplasia_2$malig_cancers_count_lifetime + (comorbs_neoplasia_2[[col_name]] == 1)
  }
  
  # Count for benign cancers
  if (col_name %in% benign_cancers) {
    comorbs_neoplasia_2$benign_cancers_count_lifetime <- comorbs_neoplasia_2$benign_cancers_count_lifetime + (comorbs_neoplasia_2[[col_name]] == 1)
  }
}

#create Y N columns for each in addition to counts

  mutate(
    all_cancers_YN_lifetime = ifelse(all_cancers_count_lifetime >= 1, 1, 0),
    malig_cancers_YN_lifetime = ifelse(malig_cancers_count_lifetime >= 1, 1, 0),
  )


#code to get to unique rows and keep the max count for each dog
#get the max count value for each of the counts for each dog 
cancer_count_summary <- comorbs_neoplasia_2 %>%
  group_by(subject_id) %>%
  summarise(
    malig_cancers_count_lifetime = if_else(all(is.na(malig_cancers_count_lifetime)), 0, max(malig_cancers_count_lifetime, na.rm = TRUE)),
    all_cancers_count_lifetime = if_else(all(is.na(all_cancers_count_lifetime)), 0, max(all_cancers_count_lifetime, na.rm = TRUE)),
    malig_cancers_count_lifetime = if_else(all(is.na(malig_cancers_count_lifetime)), 0, max(malig_cancers_count_lifetime, na.rm = TRUE)),
    all_cancers_count_lifetime = if_else(all(is.na(all_cancers_count_lifetime)), 0, max(all_cancers_count_lifetime, na.rm = TRUE)),

    malig_cancers_YN_lifetime = if_else(all(is.na(malig_cancers_YN_lifetime)), 0, max(malig_cancers_YN_lifetime, na.rm = TRUE)),
    all_cancers_YN_lifetime = if_else(all(is.na(all_cancers_YN_lifetime)), 0, max(all_cancers_YN_lifetime, na.rm = TRUE)),
    malig_cancers_YN_lifetime = if_else(all(is.na(malig_cancers_YN_lifetime)), 0, max(malig_cancers_YN_lifetime, na.rm = TRUE)),
    all_cancers_YN_lifetime = if_else(all(is.na(all_cancers_YN_lifetime)), 0, max(all_cancers_YN_lifetime, na.rm = TRUE)),
    
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
#NSAID
NSAID_ever<- medications %>%
  mutate(NSAID_ever = apply(select(., medication_name, medication_name_specify, medication_ingredients), 
                            1, 
                            function(row) {
                              # Check each column in the row for a match with NSAID_names
                              any(tolower(str_trim(row)) %in% tolower(str_trim(NSAID_names)))
                            })) %>%
  mutate(NSAID_ever= ifelse(NSAID_ever, 1, 0)) %>%
  arrange(subject_id, desc(NSAID_ever)) %>%  # Ensure NSAID_5y = 1 rows come first
  distinct(subject_id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%  # Keep first row for each subject_id
  select(subject_id, NSAID_ever)

#steroid
steroid_ever<- medications %>%
  mutate(steroid_ever = apply(select(., medication_name, medication_name_specify, medication_ingredients), 
                            1, 
                            function(row) {
                              # Check each column in the row for a match with NSAID_names
                              any(tolower(str_trim(row)) %in% tolower(str_trim(steroid_names)))
                            })) %>%
  mutate(steroid_ever = ifelse(steroid_ever, 1, 0)) %>%
  arrange(subject_id, desc(steroid_ever)) %>%  # Ensure NSAID_ever = 1 rows come first
  distinct(subject_id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%  # Keep first row for each subject_id
  select(subject_id, steroid_ever)
#fenbendazole
fenbendazole_ever <- medications %>%
  mutate(fenbendazole_ever = apply(select(., medication_name, medication_name_specify, medication_ingredients), 
                            1, 
                            function(row) {
                              # Check each column in the row for a match with NSAID_names
                              any(tolower(str_trim(row)) %in% tolower(str_trim(fenbendazole_names)))
                            })) %>%
  mutate(fenbendazole_ever = ifelse(fenbendazole_ever, 1, 0)) %>%
  arrange(subject_id, desc(fenbendazole_ever)) %>%  # Ensure NSAID_ever = 1 rows come first
  distinct(subject_id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%  # Keep first row for each subject_id
  select(subject_id, fenbendazole_ever)
```

## Reproduction variables

Reproductive features use the annual female and male reproductive-history
tables plus neuter status and dates from `Data/dog_profile.csv`. The heat-detail
table is not used here because `heat_date` has substantially less coverage than
the annual `heat_last_year` indicator.

The first-heat age is therefore the dog's age at the first questionnaire that
reported a heat in the preceding year; it is an approximate reporting age, not
an exact heat date. `heat_reporting_years` counts distinct study years with a
positive `heat_last_year` response and must not be interpreted as the literal
number of heats.

Pregnancy and mating are defined as ever recorded, regardless of neuter status,
because some dogs are never neutered. Pregnancy is not applicable to male dogs,
and mating is not applicable to female dogs. Male mating uses either a positive
annual intact-breeding response or the neutered-ever-bred response.

Neuter age, time between neutering and the cohort endpoint, and age at endpoint
are derived from recorded dates. The workflow stops rather than replacing
negative intervals with zero. In the current data, dogs `094-000441` and
`094-023124` have neuter dates before birth. Ten dogs have neuter dates after
the MCT endpoint; four of these also affect lymphoma: `094-006352`,
`094-000677`, `094-026390`, and `094-027529`. These source/cohort dates must
be resolved before accepting new analysis datasets.

```{r}
source(here::here("R", "reproduction.R"))

repro_hx_female <- read.csv(
  here::here("Data", "reproductive_history_female.csv")
)
repro_hx_male <- read.csv(
  here::here("Data", "reproductive_history_male.csv")
)
profile <- read.csv(here::here("Data", "dog_profile.csv"))

dog_pop_deprivation_enviro_smoking_sleep_lifestyle_all_house_location_comorbs_meds_NSAID_steroid_neutering3 <-
  build_reproduction_features(
    dog_pop_deprivation_enviro_smoking_sleep_lifestyle_all_house_location_comorbs_meds_NSAID_steroid,
    profile,
    repro_hx_female,
    repro_hx_male
  )
```

## Weight and height data 5y prior to endpoint

Physical examination records from the endpoint study year and the five preceding
study years are used. The primary summaries require at least five examination
rows, preserving the established threshold; the `any_records` medians remain
available when fewer records exist. Weight is converted from pounds to kg using
0.453 and height from inches to cm using 2.54. Converted summaries are left
missing for dogs younger than 18 months at the endpoint (six dogs in the legacy
notes). Where BCS values tie for the mode, the maximum tied value is used.

```{r}
source(here::here("R", "weight.R"))

dog_weight <- read.csv(here::here("Data/exam_physical.csv"))
dog_pop_deprivation_enviro_smoking_sleep_lifestyle_all_house_location_comorbs_meds_NSAID_steroid_neutering3_weight4_unique <-
  build_weight_features(
    dog_pop_deprivation_enviro_smoking_sleep_lifestyle_all_house_location_comorbs_meds_NSAID_steroid_neutering3,
    dog_weight
  )
```

```{r}
write.csv(dog_pop_deprivation_enviro_smoking_sleep_lifestyle_all_house_location_comorbs_meds_NSAID_steroid_neutering3_weight4_unique,here::here("Output/GRLS_lymphoma_variables_dataset_interim.csv"))
```

## Activity

This feature set follows the original classification work in
`Code/GRLS activity classifcation method_modified.qmd`. The questionnaire
changed after study year 2, so the two periods retain their established scoring
systems:

- study years 0--2 combine reported walk and aerobic duration, frequency, and
  intensity;
- study year 3 onward scores activity frequency and pace, because duration is
  not collected in the later format;
- the overview questionnaire supplies the whole-period activity assessment.

Every activity record after the dog's endpoint is ignored before any summary is
calculated. Full-date source tables are compared with `end_date`; the
month-resolution overview table is compared with the endpoint month. The
five-year summaries use records from the endpoint study year and the five
preceding study years.

The SY3+ and overview fields are ordinary means of their scored records. This
corrects the legacy calculation that divided those means by record count a
second time. `avg_frequency_5y_prior_endpoint` is calculated from the combined
early and later records in the five-year window; it is not replaced by the
all-SY3 mean.

For ordinal modes (the early recommendation categories and, in the lymphoma
schema, overview activity score), the maximum value is used where modal values
tie. This is the documented ordinal tie rule; nominal modes elsewhere in the
pipeline continue to use `multiple`.

```{r}
source(here::here("R", "activity.R"))

activity_sy1_2 <- read.csv(
  here::here("Data/activity_details_through_SY2.csv")
)
activity_sy3_beyond <- read.csv(
  here::here("Data/activity_details_SY3_beyond.csv")
)
activity_overview <- read.csv(here::here("Data/activity_overview.csv"))

dog_pop_deprivation_enviro_smoking_sleep_lifestyle_all_house_location_comorbs_meds_NSAID_steroid_neutering3_weight4_unique <-
  dog_pop_deprivation_enviro_smoking_sleep_lifestyle_all_house_location_comorbs_meds_NSAID_steroid_neutering3_weight4_unique |>
  dplyr::select(-c(year_in_study.x, year_in_study.y, record_date.y))

dog_pop_deprivation_enviro_smoking_sleep_lifestyle_all_house_location_comorbs_meds_NSAID_steroid_neutering3_weight4_activity_endpoint_activity <-
  build_activity_features(
    dog_pop_deprivation_enviro_smoking_sleep_lifestyle_all_house_location_comorbs_meds_NSAID_steroid_neutering3_weight4_unique,
    activity_sy1_2,
    activity_sy3_beyond,
    activity_overview
  )
```

## Tidying up columns for final df

Dates and endpoint fields retain genuine `NA` values (for example, a dog that
was never withdrawn). Missing values in analysis feature columns are written as
`records_not_available`. The feature selection is name-based so it cannot
silently shift when an upstream column is added or removed.

CSV row names are disabled; spreadsheet-style `X` index columns are not part of
the analysis dataset.

```{r}
source(here::here("R", "final_dataset.R"))

dog_pop_deprivation_enviro_smoking_sleep_lifestyle_all_house_location_comorbs_meds_NSAID_steroid_neutering3_weight4_activity_endpoint_activity_tidied <-
  finalise_cancer_dataset(
    dog_pop_deprivation_enviro_smoking_sleep_lifestyle_all_house_location_comorbs_meds_NSAID_steroid_neutering3_weight4_activity_endpoint_activity,
    case_column = "lymphoma"
  )

write.csv(
  dog_pop_deprivation_enviro_smoking_sleep_lifestyle_all_house_location_comorbs_meds_NSAID_steroid_neutering3_weight4_activity_endpoint_activity_tidied,
  here::here("Output/GRLS_lymphoma_variables_dataset.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
